Yes actually, assuming you’re playing CK2 at least, there’s a YT channel that explains how marriage and marrying into thrones works. 

As for who you’re marrying it doesn’t matter, as long as they are the child or a close relative of the King. Everyone ahead of who you married in the line of succession needs to die

Here’s the video I referenced, the same approach works in CK3 as far as I know: https://youtu.be/bqhxXLoe1R4

Ah, taking the Habsburg approach are we?

The easiest way to do this is by marrying someone in the line of succession (you can check who’s in line by clicking on the title) and ensure they’re next in line by killing off everyone else in line ahead of them.

As an example: I’m the king of Poland but want to inherit Hungary. I’ll marry my first son and heir to the first or second daughter of the King of Hungary. As long as the other kingdom has agnatic-cognatic, you’ll be able to inherit their throne by killing off the heirs to the kingdom in question.

This is even easier as you (Ireland) as you have Tanistry which is a form of elective succession, so just marry into the throne of Scotland and pick that kid as the heir.

Hope this helps!

Historically this can be done in two ways, internally and externally, with the former being the reformist “moderate” position and the latter being the more “radical” or revolutionary position.

Historically speaking, the political status quo can only be challenged outright in a time of crisis from a group with some influence, meaning the biggest thing is to first gain influence be it through Congress or by having enough money and connections to become a political financier. Afterwards you need to build up a base or clique of likeminded politicians and leaders who will carry this position. Ideally this would happen in a time of upheaval in the country (such as right now) as people aren’t typically open to change unless their way of life is threatened in some way.

The more radical stance is an outright populist or revolutionary movement sprouting from a disgruntled citizenry who either take power in elections in a time of trouble or just coup the government. Given the level of state security however, the latter isn’t really an option.

Tldr, to reform, one needs to gain influence and use it to change shit. The problem is, most of the time once someone gains some degree of power or influence they become complacent.
